messages:
Nora Blake: Quick alert on HarborLytics onboarding — p95 for /complete is drifting to ~2.4s and token spend is ~41% above their projection. They have a chat-first UX with lots of short queries (~30–90 tokens) and periodic report-generation jobs. Proactive recommendation: 1) route short queries to a tiny quantized path (int4), 2) enable short-lived prefix/KV caching for session state, 3) schedule Dedicated capacity for their daily peak (14:00–18:00 UTC). Thoughts?

Ethan Wu: Can we get a traffic breakdown and a couple of failing traces? Also need to confirm whether the client can emit a header to signal "interactive_turn".

Nora Blake: Traces & distribution: https://redwood.app/insights/harborlytics/onboard/821250 - majority of calls are sub-80 tokens. HarborLytics engineering can add header interactive_turn=true, but we should offer server-side token_count fallback.

Priyanka Rao: For renewal posture, let's frame this as a low-friction pilot: 24h compact path for short queries, safety net fallback, and clear ROI slide. I'll prepare a renewal note with conservative/expected/optimistic savings.

Ethan Wu: On the runtime side, recommend deterministic routing by token_count <= 80 or header.interactive_turn == true. Fallback cascade: harbor-compact-1.3b-int4 -> harbor-compact-1.3b-int8 -> harbor-standard-3b. Also add prefix cache ttl=180s and a small batching window for compact path.

Nora Blake: Draft routing policy to hand to runtime:
```json
{
  "route": "/complete",
  "selector": "header.interactive_turn == true || token_count <= 80",
  "primary_models": ["harbor-compact-1.3b-int4", "harbor-compact-1.3b-int8"],
  "fallback": "harbor-standard-3b",
  "cache": {"prefix_kv": true, "ttl_seconds": 180},
  "dedicated_window": "14:00-18:00 UTC",
  "observability": ["latency_p95","token_delta","regression_rate"]
}
```

Ethan Wu: @eng-runtime-bot can you schedule a 3% traffic canary for 24h starting 2026-09-15T14:00:00Z? Add monitors: p95 latency, 5xx, token_delta, and regression_rate vs QA harness with pass threshold <=5% regressions.

eng-runtime-bot: Canary scheduled: job_id=harbor-canary-821250-01, start=2026-09-15T14:00:00Z, traffic=3%, duration=24h. Monitoring hooks configured (latency_p95, 5xx, token_delta, regression_rate). Will post completion and periodic summaries. :gear:

Priyanka Rao: QA plan: I'll assemble a 30-case harness focused on short-turn fidelity, entity retention, and edge-case prompts (dates, currency, nested lists). QA-bot, please run regression tests at canary end.

QA-bot: Received harness request. Will execute comparison against baseline model at canary completion and report pass/fail and top-5 failure examples. Gate: regression_rate <= 5% and no critical hallucinations.

Sales Ops: Adding a calendar hold on the account timeline and flagging renewal team to wait for pilot numbers before outreach.

Ethan Wu: If the canary is green, propose ramp plan: 3% -> 15% -> 50% over 48h with rollback triggers: p95 increase >10% or regression_rate >5% sustained for 15m. Also recommend we present both latency and token-savings numbers in the renewal slide to show tangible impact.

Nora Blake: I'll update the renewal risk tracker (status: pilot-scheduled) and schedule a 30-min enablement with HarborLytics PMs for the day after canary completes to capture qualitative feedback.

Priyanka Rao: I'll draft the ROI slide and include a short appendix about fallback behavior and rollback plan for legal/ops sign-off.

Ethan Wu: Minor note — we should also compute worst-case quality delta (top-3 failure examples) so CS can be transparent. I'll run sim estimates and post by EOD.

Nora Blake: Thanks team. Keeping this thread as the single source of truth for pilot artifacts and results. :white_check_mark:
